answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit anchor bond on the wharf ledger for one berth with one key. Berths go in order, so attackers cannot pick empty berths to dodge cost. Each new anchor pays a ripple charge of 2 credits per moored anchor. A gale sweep recounts the ledger, burning bond plus charge on a copied key or mismatched quill receipt; clean anchors recover bonds. The k-th fake risks 60+2(k-1) credits, the 1,000th 2,058, and 1,000 fakes 1,059,000. A rented anchor fails: its key mismatches the renter's quill receipt, so the sweep burns the bond. An honest identity risks only one bond.
